clue.text: One tweeting of passion in sport

indicators.note: in says the word for passion sits inside the word for sport

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
heat is passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: A spectator gets carried away by passion while watching a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' is the verb, as in sporting a hat. A wheatear is a small songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small chat-like songbird, and birds are the creatures that tweet.

clue.text: Old film director, Oscar recipient?

definitions.meaning: Michael ..., the British director of Death Wish
anyone who wins an Oscar; the question mark marks it as an example

explanation.walkthrough: Michael Winner (1935-2013) was a British film director, best known for Death Wish.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a director doubles as the general word for anyone who takes a prize such as an Academy Award.

clue.text: Whole piece from composer, it needs going over

indicators.note: going over says the hidden letters are read backwards
from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musician says a composer's work needs another look before it is complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes ERITNE out of 'composer, it needs' (the draft left 'from' as a link word, though it signals the hidden word); 'going over' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means complete, all in one piece, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Time left to stop draw in Championship

indicators.note: to stop means plug a gap, so these letters go inside the word for draw

parts.note: a draw in a match is a tie

explanation.surface: A match runs out of time just before it can finish level in a title race.
explanation.definitionFit: A title in sport is a championship won, as in holding the world title.

clue.text: Liberal going after a job meets European advocate

indicators.note: going after says the letter for Liberal is placed behind A POST

parts.note: a post is a job

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician chasing a job meets a European campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names Liberal first, but 'going after' puts its L behind A POST.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a keen supporter of a cause, a synonym for advocate in its noun sense.

clue.text: Insensitive practice by old broadband provider

parts.note: BT, British Telecom, supplies broadband in the UK
use is practice, as in custom and use

explanation.surface: A complaint that an old internet company's way of doing things is thoughtless.
explanation.walkthrough: BT is Britain's main telephone and broadband company.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand or notice, so dull or unperceptive.

clue.text: Bird in Belgium, pale-coloured, needs feeding

indicators.note: feeding means putting into, so the word for needs goes inside the other letters

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
wan means pale
lacks means needs or is without

explanation.surface: A pale, hungry bird in Belgium wants food.
explanation.definitionFit: The black swan is a large waterbird native to Australia with dark plumage.

clue.text: Shunning area, relative wound up being neglected

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so the letter for area is dropped from the relative

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
wound up means finished, ended

explanation.surface: A relative who avoided a place ended up feeling ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shunning' drops the A of area from AUNT, leaving UNT; 'wound up' is ENDED, not a winding of any letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untended is left uncared for, which is the state of being neglected.

clue.text: Opponents speak over first writer

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first pieces above the letters for first

parts.note: E and S, East and South, are opposing partners at bridge
to say is to speak
1ST is the abbreviation for first, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Rivals address the opening speaker of a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge East and South sit against each other, so ES is a crossword pair for opponents; 1ST is read with the figure 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist is an author of essays, a kind of writer.

clue.text: Swimming race Thai regularly enters

indicators.note: enters says the picked letters go inside the word for race

parts.note: a nation is a people or race

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of Thai, the first and third

explanation.surface: A Thai swimmer competes regularly in races.
explanation.definitionFit: Natation is the formal term for the act or art of swimming.

clue.text: Sticks with sweets, difficult to give up

indicators.note: to give up means to let go of, so the letters for difficult are taken out

parts.note: pastilles are small sweets
ill can mean difficult or bad, as in ill-tempered

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hard to give up sweets and sticks with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks with' looks like a phrase; 'with' is only a link. ILL for difficult is the old sense seen in ill at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: To paste is to glue something, so pastes means fixes on with adhesive.

clue.text: Story of mine that's originally hard to follow

indicators.note: to follow puts the later letters after MY

parts.note: my means belonging to me, of mine

indicators.note: originally points to the start of that's, its opening letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone says a tale of theirs is hard to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a traditional tale or legend, a fictional narrative.

clue.text: Make style fresh in an enthusiastic manner

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters of style are made into something new

explanation.surface: An instruction to update a look with eager energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means with serious, sincere intent, an adverb of zeal and keenness.

clue.text: Unconventional family occasionally okay

parts.note: kin are family

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only the second and fourth letters of okay are taken

explanation.surface: An unusual family is fine some of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinky means odd or bizarre, often of sexual tastes, so out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Arrogance of assistant having succeeded ousting American

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so the letter for succeeded replaces the one for American

parts.note: an aide is an assistant
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogy

explanation.surface: An aide who got promoted over an American turned arrogant.
explanation.walkthrough: Side here is the old noun for swagger, as in putting on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Side is British slang for pretentious airs or conceit, a dated sense of haughty behaviour.

clue.text: Noticing Dicky hosting ball under an assumed name

indicators.note: hosting means having a guest inside, so the ball shape goes within
dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters of noticing are jumbled

parts.note: O is a round ball shape

explanation.surface: Someone spots a disguised guest at a dance under a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky is British slang for weak or unreliable, as in a dicky heart. The ball is the round O, not a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Going incognito means concealing one's identity, typically by using a false name.

clue.text: Member of Parliament is wearing that woman's bloomers!

indicators.note: being worn means being inside, so the bird goes within the word for that woman's

parts.note: hers means belonging to that woman
a group of owls is called a parliament, so one owl is a member

explanation.surface: A politician is caught wearing a woman's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: A parliament is the collective noun for owls. Bloomers are blunders as well as knickers, and the exclamation mark enjoys that.
explanation.definitionFit: Howlers and bloomers are both informal words for embarrassing blunders or glaring mistakes.

clue.text: Training cost rose for motorcycles

indicators.note: training means shaping or drilling, so the letters of cost rose are put into new order

explanation.surface: Learner riders' lesson fees have risen.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor scooters are light motorbikes with small wheels and a step-through frame.

clue.text: Old man about to stuff tablet in dog

indicators.note: to stuff means to fill, so the tablet goes inside the other letters

parts.note: pa is a father, one's old man
on means about, as in a book on birds
a pill is a tablet

explanation.surface: Father gets ready to hide a pill in the dog's food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: The papillon is a small toy spaniel breed named for its butterfly-shaped ears.

clue.text: Opportunist placing sign across hotel

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the star sign sits either side of the hotel letter

parts.note: Cancer is a sign of the zodiac
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A chancer puts a notice up across a hotel front.
explanation.walkthrough: The sign is of the zodiac, not a placard.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is a British informal word for someone who takes risks to grab advantage.

clue.text: Scrap in lorry leaving tip?

indicators.note: leaving tip means the front letter is taken off

parts.note: lorry is the British word for a truck

explanation.surface: Junk in a lorry is being taken to the dump.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip is a British rubbish dump, which suits the scrap in the surface. A ruck is a brawl, and a loose scrum in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruck is a rough tussle or brawl, an informal word for a fight or scrap.

clue.text: National force put before local

indicators.note: put before places the force letter ahead of the pub

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
a local is a British name for a neighbourhood pub, an inn

explanation.surface: A national police force takes priority over a local one.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain one's local is the nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a citizen of Finland, so a national of that country.

clue.text: Waste battered food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... money or time away is to squander it
second meaning: a piece of fruit or meat fried in batter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests throwing away food, but the two parts are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as a verb for squandering and a noun for a fried, batter-coated morsel.

clue.text: Any number going out for drink

parts.note: N stands for any number in mathematics

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of going are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crowd heading out for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going out' reads as a night out, but 'out' rearranges GOING.
explanation.definitionFit: A noggin is a small measure of spirits, usually a quarter of a pint.

clue.text: Cousins tiling houses impress

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Relatives who do roofing make an impression with their work on houses.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to fix it firmly in someone's mind, to stamp or press it in.

clue.text: Outstanding oarsmanship right away

indicators.note: away means gone, so the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: rowing is the skill of using oars

explanation.surface: Praise for excellent rowing straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means excellent in the surface but unpaid here.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing means still to be paid, as is a debt left outstanding.

clue.text: Movie I watch on streaming around noon

indicators.note: around places the rearranged letters on either side of the noon letter
streaming means flowing freely, so the letters of I watch on are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone streams a film at lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinatown is the 1974 Roman Polanski film noir starring Jack Nicholson.

clue.text: Gunners line up during morning panic

indicators.note: during means within a period, so the turned letters sit inside the morning

parts.note: AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: Soldiers fall in at dawn amid alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery, RA, are the gunners of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is a sudden fear or anxiety, which is close to panic.

clue.text: City banker in Yorkshire almost eats large cake

indicators.note: eats means takes in, so the large letter goes inside

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the river goes

parts.note: a banker is a river, something with banks; the Aire flows through Leeds

explanation.surface: A City banker on a Yorkshire trip gorges on a large cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a river, a thing with banks: the Aire, a Yorkshire river, cut short to AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Frank rigs that broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of rigs that are rearranged

explanation.surface: Frank fixes the results of a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a name, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means honest and direct, which is a synonym of frank.

clue.text: Former magistrate reportedly that triggers 26 Down?

indicators.note: reportedly means by word of mouth, so the magistrate's title is heard, not seen

parts.note: a censor was a magistrate of ancient Rome who kept the census

explanation.surface: A retired magistrate is said to set off the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: In ancient Rome a censor was a magistrate who took the census and policed morals.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensor is a detector, the device that sets off an alarm when it senses smoke or movement.

clue.text: Wrong about student touring Adriatic resort shortly

indicators.note: touring means going all round, so the other letters circle the cut resort

parts.note: CA, circa, means about

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter of the resort goes

parts.note: Rimini is an Italian seaside resort on the Adriatic
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A student touring an Italian beach resort goes astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The L of a learner driver stands for student.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminal can mean morally wrong or deplorable, as in a criminal waste.
